svg.text: asX-ray (Simple Surgeries): how the system fits together
A patient watches a procedure in 3D, points at parts to learn about them, and asks a chatbot that answers from our own facts and moves the 3D view. Personal details are replaced on the device first.
Your browser (apps/frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, three.js)
Landing · Walkthrough list · FAQs · Login and sign up · Devices lab
Saves which step the patient is on
Username and password sign-up and login
A route guard protects the walkthrough pages
Delivery catheter, balloon and new valve built
Part picker: hover shows a name, click pins it
Scene director: applies the chat's scene_actions
Slow / Fast switch with a paid-service warning
Shows the answer, sources, a safety note and a
question for the care team, plus follow-ups
Spoken audio cannot be redacted on the device
Privacy guard (on the device, before anything is sent)
Always on. Finds SSN, birth date,
A small AI model that runs in the
names and places the rules miss
A last scan blocks the send if
Real name, birth date and SSN stay here
The exact text that was sent, never real values
Convex Auth: usernames and hashed passwords.
Names and emails never reach the chatbot or any model
Scope gate and emergency rules (medicine, diagnosis, tricks
get a fixed reply; no model call)
Find sources: keyword search + vector search
The model writes a JSON answer (Slow or Fast)
Grounding check: numbers and terms must appear in our facts
Keep only scene_actions that pass zod and exist in the
Reply: message, sources, scene_actions, safety note
Upload the recording, transcribe it, delete the audio
right away (also on errors, plus an hourly cleanup)
84 short facts (80 from the team's TAVR document),
with a vector index. The pipeline reads these
Latest 6 messages + a short summary of earlier ones
Deleted when the page closes; idle ones purged hourly

zod schemas (ChatResponse, SceneAction, Procedure, Structure) and fixtures (TAVR steps, eye steps, knowledge facts). The frontend, the backend and the tests all use them, so a part id like "aortic_valve" means the same thing everywhere.
